stem: Fill in the blank: The degree of dissociation is defined as the fraction of a mole of reactant that has ______ at equilibrium.
Fill in the blank: The ______, represented as Q, is calculated in the same way as the equilibrium constant, but from concentrations at any point in time, not necessarily at equilibrium.
Fill in the blank: If Q c > K c , the reaction will proceed in the ______ direction to reach equilibrium.
Fill in the blank: The relationship between the equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy is given by the equation ΔG = −RT ln ______.
Fill in the blank: If the reaction is exergonic (ΔG < 0), the reaction proceeds in the ______ direction.
True or false: The degree of dissociation can never exceed 1.
True or false: If Q c = K c , the system is already at equilibrium.
True or false: If Q c < K c , the reaction will proceed in the reverse direction to reach equilibrium.
True or false: A negative value for ΔG indicates that the reaction is spontaneous.
True or false: The reaction quotient Q and the equilibrium constant K are calculated using the same equation.
True or false: If Q > K at a given temperature, the reaction will shift toward the reactants.

Match the column. Column-I: (A) Degree of Dissociation (B) Reaction Quotient (C) Direction of Equilibrium (D) K c (E) Gibbs Free Energy Column-II: (p) Gives the spontaneous direction of a reaction (q) Ratio of concentration of products to reactants at any point in time (r) Fraction of a mole of reactant that has dissociated at equilibrium (s) If greater than Q, the reaction proceeds in the forward direction (t) If it is negative, the reaction is spontaneous
In which of the following cases does the reaction go farthest to completion? (a) K = 10 2 (b) K = 10 (c) K = 10 −2 (d) K = 1
Standard free energy change for an equilibrium is zero; the value of K p is (a) Zero (b) 1 (c) 2 (d) 100
The value of ΔG° for the phosphorylation of glucose in glycolysis is 13.8 kJ/mol. The value of K c at 298 K will be (a) 3.81×10 −2 (b) 3.81×10 −3 (c) 3.81×10 −5 (d) 3.81×10 −4

For the reaction PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g) ⇌ PCl 5 (g), the value of K c at 250 °C is 26 mol litre −1 . The value of K p at this temperature will be: (a) 0.61 atm −1 (b) 0.57 atm −1 (c) 0.83 atm −1 (d) 0.46 atm −1

The reaction quotient (Q) for the reaction N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) is given by Q = [NH 3 ] 2 /([N 2 ][H 2 ] 3 ). The reaction will proceed from right to left if (a) Q = K c (b) Q < K c (c) Q > K c (d) Q = 0
The equilibrium constant K c for the reaction N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) is 0.286 at 500 °C. Calculate K c and K p for the reaction 2NH 3 (g) ⇌ N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g).

The equilibrium constant K c for the reaction COCl 2 (g) ⇌ CO(g) + Cl 2 (g) is 0.08 at a certain temperature. If the equilibrium concentration of COCl 2 is 0.10 M, what are the equilibrium concentrations of CO and Cl 2 ?

Calculate K c for the equilibrium process CO 2 (g) + H 2 (g) ⇌ CO(g) + H 2 O(g). At equilibrium the reaction system contains 3.52 g of CO 2 , 1.4 g of CO, 0.08 g of H 2 and 0.72 g of H 2 O. (Atomic masses: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)

A mixture of 3.8 moles of NO and 0.924 moles of CO 2 was allowed to react in a 1.0 L container. The equilibrium mixture contains 0.124 mole of CO. Calculate K c for the reaction NO(g) + CO 2 (g) ⇌ NO 2 (g) + CO(g).

key: (c) Products predominate and reaction proceeds nearly to completion
stem: What does a very large equilibrium constant (K >> 1) indicate? (a) The reaction hardly proceeds (b) The reaction is at equilibrium (c) Products predominate and reaction proceeds nearly to completion (d) Reactants predominate

key: (b) Reaction will proceed in reverse direction
stem: What does it mean if Q > K for a reaction? (a) Reaction is at equilibrium (b) Reaction will proceed in reverse direction (c) Reaction will proceed forward (d) Reaction is irreversible

Which of the following best describes the use of the reaction quotient Q? (a) Predicting rate of reaction (b) Calculating activation energy (c) Predicting direction of reaction (d) Measuring temperature change
What is the condition for a reaction mixture to be at equilibrium? (a) Q > K (b) Q < K (c) Q = K (d) K = 0

Which step is not part of calculating equilibrium concentrations? (a) Setting up a table with initial and equilibrium values (b) Solving for x using equilibrium expressions (c) Adding heat to the system (d) Substituting values into the equilibrium constant expression
For the reaction H 2 (g) + I 2 (g) ⇌ 2HI(g), at a certain stage the concentrations are [H 2 ] = 0.1 M, [I 2 ] = 0.2 M and [HI] = 0.4 M. What is the value of Q? (a) 4 (b) 2 (c) 6 (d) 8
If the value of the equilibrium constant K for a reaction is 10 and Q = 2, what is the direction of the reaction? (a) Backward (b) Forward (c) At equilibrium (d) Cannot say
If for a reaction ΔG° = −5.7 kJ/mol and T = 298 K, what is the approximate value of K? (Use R = 8.314 J/mol·K) (a) 1 (b) 10 (c) 100 (d) 1000
What is ΔG for a reaction where ΔG° = 0 and Q = 10? (Use R = 8.314 J/mol·K, T = 298 K) (a) 0 (b) 5.7 kJ/mol (c) −5.7 kJ/mol (d) 2.5 kJ/mol
At equilibrium, if [A] = 1 mol/L, [B] = 2 mol/L, and the reaction A ⇌ B has K c = 2, what is the value of Q? (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 4 (d) 0.5

At 298 K, the standard Gibbs free energy change (ΔG°) for a reaction is −5.7 kJ/mol. Calculate the equilibrium constant K, and then find Q if ΔG at this condition becomes 0. (a) K = 100, Q = 100 (b) K = 100, Q = 1 (c) K = 10, Q = 10 (d) K = 1, Q = 10

The equilibrium constant K c for a reaction is 49. If the initial concentrations of H 2 and I 2 are 1 M each and no HI is present, find the equilibrium concentration of HI. (a) 1.5 M (b) 1.4 M (c) 1.9 M (d) 2.0 M

A reaction has ΔG° = −4.6 kJ/mol. Calculate K at 300 K and then determine ΔG if Q = 10. (R = 8.314 J/mol·K) (a) K = 20, ΔG = −3.0 kJ/mol (b) K = 100, ΔG = −5.0 kJ/mol (c) K = 6.3, ΔG = 1.14 kJ/mol (d) K = 5, ΔG = −3.5 kJ/mol
For a reaction, Q = 5 and K = 0.5 at 298 K. Calculate ΔG using two steps. (R = 8.314 J/mol·K) (a) 4.0 kJ/mol (b) 5.7 kJ/mol (c) 7.0 kJ/mol (d) 10.2 kJ/mol
For the reaction H 2 + I 2 ⇌ 2HI, if K c = 100 and [HI] = 0.8 M at equilibrium, calculate [H 2 ] and [I 2 ] assuming they are equal. (a) 0.1 M (b) 0.08 M (c) 0.05 M (d) 0.2 M

For the reaction Cu(s) + 2Ag + (aq) ⇌ Cu 2+ (aq) + 2Ag(s), the equilibrium constant K c is given by (a) [Cu 2+ ][Ag] 2 /([Cu][Ag + ] 2 ) (b) [Cu 2+ ][2Ag]/([Cu][2Ag + ]) (c) [Cu 2+ ]/[Ag + ] 2 (d) [Ag + ] 2 /[Cu 2+ ]

The equilibrium constant for the reaction CuSO 4 ·5H 2 O(s) ⇌ CuSO 4 ·3H 2 O(s) + 2H 2 O(g) is equal to (a) [CuSO 4 ·3H 2 O][H 2 O] 2 /[CuSO 4 ·5H 2 O] (b) [CuSO 4 ·3H 2 O]/[CuSO 4 ·5H 2 O] (c) [H 2 O] 2 (d) [H 2 O]
Reactions that have standard free energy changes less than zero always have an equilibrium constant (a) Equal to unity (b) Greater than unity (c) Less than unity (d) Zero
A large positive value of ΔG° corresponds to which of these? (a) Small positive K (b) Small negative K (c) Large positive K (d) Large negative K

Phosphorus pentachloride dissociates as follows in a closed reaction vessel: PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g). If the total pressure at equilibrium of the reaction mixture is P and the degree of dissociation of PCl 5 is x, the partial pressure of PCl 3 will be (a) [x/(x+1)]P (b) [2x/(1−x)]P (c) [x/(x−1)]P (d) [x/(1−x)]P 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2006 Solution ↗

In a chemical equilibrium A + B ⇌ C + D, when one mole each of the two reactants are mixed, 0.6 mole each of the products are formed. The equilibrium constant calculated is (a) 1 (b) 0.36 (c) 2.25 (d) 4/9
The equilibrium constant (K) of a reaction may be written as (a) K = e −ΔG/RT (b) K = e −ΔG°/RT (c) K = e −ΔH/RT (d) K = e −ΔH°/RT
Which of the following statements is correct for a reversible process in a state of equilibrium? (a) ΔG° = −2.30 RT log K (b) ΔG° = 2.30 RT log K (c) ΔG = −2.30 RT log K (d) ΔG = 2.30 RT log K

For the reaction 3A + B ⇌ 2C + D, the equilibrium concentrations of A, B and C are 0.03, 0.01 and 0.008 mol L −1 respectively. What is the initial concentration of A? (a) 0.004 (b) 0.026 (c) 0.042 (d) 0.018

For the reaction 2NO 2 (g) ⇌ 2NO(g) + O 2 (g), K c = 1.8×10 −6 at 184 °C and R = 0.083 litre-atm K −1 mol −1 . When K p and K c are compared at 184 °C, it is found that: (a) K p > K c (b) K p < K c (c) K p = K c (d) K p ≤ K c 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2005 Solution ↗

For NH 4 HS(s) ⇌ NH 3 (g) + H 2 S(g), the observed pressure for the reaction mixture in equilibrium is 1.12 atm at 106 °C. The value of K p for the reaction is: (a) 3.136 atm 2 (b) 0.3136 atm 2 (c) 31.36 atm 2 (d) 6.98 atm 2
For the system A(g) + 2B(g) ⇌ C(g), the equilibrium concentrations are A = 0.06 mol L −1 , B = 0.12 mol L −1 , C = 0.216 mol L −1 . The K for the reaction is (a) 250 (b) 416 (c) 4×10 −3 (d) 125
15 g mole of H 2 react with 5.2 g mole of I 2 to form 10 g mole of HI. Calculate the equilibrium constant for the reaction.

40% of a mixture of 0.2 mole of N 2 and 0.6 mole of H 2 react to give NH 3 according to N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) at constant temperature and pressure. Then the ratio of the final volume to the initial volume of gases is: (a) 4 : 5 (b) 5 : 4 (c) 7 : 10 (d) 8 : 5

The effect of temperature on the equilibrium constant is expressed as (T 2 > T 1 ) log(K 2 /K 1 ) = (−ΔH/2.303)[1/T 2 − 1/T 1 ]. For an endothermic reaction the false statement is (a) [1/T 2 − 1/T 1 ] = positive (b) ΔH = positive (c) log K 2 > log K 1 (d) K 2 > K 1

key: (c) backward direction till it attains equilibrium
stem: For the equilibrium n-butane(g) ⇌ iso-butane(g) the equilibrium constant is 1.732 at 298 K. In a vessel at 298 K a mixture of the two gases is taken as represented by the point P in the figure, which lies on a dashed line through the origin making 75° with the n-butane axis (concentration of iso-butane on the vertical axis). Predict what will happen. (a) Immediately, above equilibrium will be set up (b) The reaction will go in the forward direction till it attains equilibrium (c) The reaction will go in the backward direction till it attains equilibrium (d) Nothing can be said

Of the following reactions (i) A ⇌ B, ΔG° = 250 kJ mol −1 ; (ii) D ⇌ E, ΔG° = 100 kJ mol −1 ; (iii) F ⇌ G, ΔG° = −150 kJ mol −1 ; (iv) M ⇌ N, ΔG° = 150 kJ mol −1 — the reaction with the largest equilibrium constant is (a) (i) (b) (ii) (c) (iii) (d) (iv)
The equilibrium PCl 5 (g) ⇌ PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g) shows that K p is 24.63 times the value of K c at a particular temperature T. Then T (in K) is: (a) 200 (b) 100 (c) 300 (d) 400

Hydrolysis of sucrose gives Sucrose + H 2 O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose. The equilibrium constant K c for the reaction is 2×10 13 at 300 K. The Gibbs energy change for this reaction at 300 K is (a) −7.64×10 4 J mol −1 (b) −7.64×10 3 J mol −1 (c) −3.32×10 4 J mol −1 (d) −3.32×10 3 J mol −1
ΔG°(HI, g) ≈ +1.7 kJ. What is the equilibrium constant at 25 °C for 2HI(g) ⇌ H 2 (g) + I 2 (g)?
ΔG° for the reaction X + Y ⇌ Z is −4.606 kcal. The equilibrium constant for the reaction at 227 °C is: (a) 100 (b) 10 (c) 2 (d) 0.01

key: (d) K p remains constant with change in P or x
stem: At constant temperature, the equilibrium constant (K p ) for the decomposition reaction N 2 O 4 ⇌ 2NO 2 is expressed by K p = 4x 2 P/(1−x 2 ), where P = pressure and x = extent of decomposition. Which of the following statements is true? (a) K p increases with increase of P (b) K p increases with increase of x (c) K p increases with decrease of x (d) K p remains constant with change in P or x

key: (a) G N₂ + 3G H₂ = 2G NH₃ at the equilibrium partial pressures
stem: For the Haber’s process for the formation of NH 3 at 298 K: N 2 + 3H 2 ⇌ 2NH 3 ; ΔH = −460 kJ. Which of the following is correct? (a) The condition for equilibrium is G N 2 + 3G H 2 = 2G NH 3 , where G is Gibbs energy per mole of the gaseous species measured at that partial pressure (b) On adding N 2 , the equilibrium will shift forward because according to the II law of thermodynamics the entropy must decrease in the direction of spontaneous reaction (c) The catalyst will increase the rate of forward reaction by 2 times and that of backward reaction by 1.5 times (d) None of these

The equilibrium constants K P 1 and K P 2 for the reactions X ⇌ 2Y and Z ⇌ P + Q respectively are in the ratio of 1 : 9. If the degrees of dissociation of X and Z are equal, then the ratio of the total pressures at these equilibria is: (a) 1 : 9 (b) 1 : 36 (c) 1 : 1 (d) 1 : 3 📝 PYQ: AIEEE 2008 Solution ↗

For the reversible reaction N 2 (g) + 3H 2 (g) ⇌ 2NH 3 (g) at 500 °C, the value of K p is 1.44×10 −5 when the partial pressure is measured in atmospheres. The corresponding value of K c , with concentration in mol litre −1 , is: (a) 1.44×10 −5 /(0.082×500) −2 (b) 1.44×10 −5 /(8.314×773) −2 (c) 1.44×10 −5 /(0.082×773) 2 (d) 1.44×10 −5 /(0.082×773) −2

Consider the following equilibria: 2NO(g) ⇌ N 2 + O 2 , K c 1 = 2.4×10 2 ; and NO(g) + ½Br 2 (g) ⇌ NOBr(g), K c 2 = 1.4. On the basis of the above data, calculate K c for the reaction ½N 2 (g) + ½O 2 (g) + ½Br 2 (g) ⇌ NOBr(g). (If the answer is x×10 −2 , find the value of x.)

Match the column (take α negligible with respect to 1). Column-I: (A) 2X(g) ⇌ Y(g) + Z(g) (B) X(g) ⇌ Y(g) + Z(g) (C) 3X(g) ⇌ Y(g) + Z(g) (D) 2X(g) ⇌ Y(g) + 2Z(g) Column-II: (P) α = 2√K c (Q) α = 3√K c (R) α = (2K c ) 1/3 (S) α = √K c (a) A—PS; B—SR; C—QP; D—RS (b) A—S; B—R; C—P; D—Q (c) A—P; B—S; C—Q; D—R (d) A—PQ; B—RS; C—SR; D—QP

key: (b) K c = K p (RT)−Δn g ; K p = K x PΔn g
stem: Passage (Q8–Q10). For a gaseous reaction aA(g) + bB(g) ⇌ cC(g) + dD(g) the equilibrium constants K c , K p and K x are represented by K c = [C] c [D] d /([A] a [B] b ), K p = (p C c p D d )/(p A a p B b ) and K x = (x C c x D d )/(x A a x B b ), where P represents the total pressure and x A the mole fraction of A. On the basis of the above work-up, select the right option. (a) K p = K c (RT) Δn g ; K x = K p (RT) Δn g (b) K c = K p (RT) −Δn g ; K p = K x P Δn g (c) K c = K x P Δn g ; K p = K x P Δn g (d) K c = K p (RT) −Δn g ; K x = K p (RT) Δn g
Passage (Q8–Q10), continued. For the reaction SO 2 Cl 2 (g) ⇌ SO 2 (g) + Cl 2 (g), K p > K x is obtained at: (a) 0.5 atm (b) 0.8 atm (c) 1 atm (d) 2 atm

Passage (Q8–Q10), continued. For the following equilibrium the relation between K c and K x (in terms of mole fraction) is: PCl 3 (g) + Cl 2 (g) ⇌ PCl 5 (g) (a) K c = K x (RT) −1 (b) K c = K x (RT) (c) K c = K x (RT/P) (d) K p = K x (P/RT)
